source_row.rationale: Sodium nitroprusside generates cyanide, and sufficient exposure can exceed detoxification capacity. Metabolic acidosis, confusion, and clinical deterioration are compatible with cyanide toxicity, making Option A correct. Thiocyanate accumulation is a distinct metabolite toxicity, methemoglobinemia is not the primary high-dose syndrome described here, and rebound hypertension does not explain the metabolic acidosis and neurologic decline.
source_row.source_detail: Warnings and Precautions, Cyanide Toxicity: nitroprusside generates dose-related cyanide; toxicity can manifest with metabolic acidosis, confusion and clinical deterioration, especially at higher exposure. DailyMed label updated 2025-11-17; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, adverse effects/interactions, reversal, monitoring and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client receiving a high-dose sodium nitroprusside infusion develops unexplained metabolic acidosis, confusion, and deterioration. Which toxicity should the nurse suspect?
